decisions.statement: The indexes answer which pages exist.
The graph answers the nodes and edges and attributes that follow from the pages.
The pages an answer rests on are worked out from the code rather than recorded as the code runs.
The answers the graph derives are a cache and never an index.
Throwing away the answers the graph derives costs only speed.
A kept answer learns that answer is stale by being asked rather than by being told.
An answer is keyed by the pages that answer rests on and marked by the code that made the answer.
The graph reaches no further than the akasha folder.
Every closure the graph answers is correct.
A closure followed in and one followed out answer the same files.
A closure is answered over the shadow a change leaves as readily as over the tree.
No file the code editor's extension host loads reaches the graph.

definition: what follows from the pages, and what each answer rests on

directives.name: Alan Approves Kinds
directives.act: Add a node, edge or attribute to the graph only where Alan has approved that kind.
directives.warrant: Every reader asks in these terms, so a kind nobody wanted becomes a word the whole system speaks.
aids: Approving the initiative is not approving a kind.
A kind replacing an old one still needs approval.

directives.name: Never Depend On Everything
directives.act: Key a question of the pages so a change reaches one key, never the whole table.
directives.warrant: A cache that never hits costs more than none, and an answer resting on everything never hits.
aids: A table is written as the rule that adjusts it, and rebuilt by adjusting from empty.
One rule used twice cannot disagree with itself.
